newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian lawmakers approve extradition bill.
newsitem.headline: Colombian lawmakers approve extradition bill.

text.p: A Colombian Senate panel on Tuesday approved a controversial constitutional reform bill intended to lift the country's's ban on extradition of drug lords and other criminals.
But the bill, approved by the constitutional affairs committee of the Senate, faced more legislative hurdles before it could become law.
While ending the ban, the bill would still rule out extradition in cases where criminals would face stiffer penalities abroad than at home.

This would effectively block extradition of any major drug lord to the United States. The maximum penalty for narcotics trafficking in Colombia was raised in Feburary to 60 years imprisonment, whereas life terms have been meted out to drug kingpins in the United States.
The bill, as approved by the Senate committee, would also block the extradition of criminals who give themselves up before they are caught.

Constitutional reforms must be approved by two consecutive sessions of Congress. The current session ends on June 20, and the bill must still be approved by the full Senate and the lower House of Representatives, before being passed on to the next session of Congress that will be installed on July 20.
